title: Academic Integrity Policy
content:
The University of Northbridge hereby adopts the Academic Integrity Policy effective 1 September 2024, superseding the prior policy dated 12 January 2023. The policy is issued by the Office of Academic Affairs under the authority of the Board of Trustees and is available to all students, faculty, and staff on the university’s public document repository (URL: https://unb.edu/policies/academicintegrity). It establishes a uniform framework for defining, preventing, and addressing violations of academic integrity, including plagiarism, fabrication, falsification, and cheating on examinations and assignments. The policy references the 2024‑25 Academic Calendar, specifically the “Academic Integrity” section of the Student Handbook (Section 3.4), and aligns with the Council for Higher Education’s national standards for scholarly conduct.

Section 1.0 – Scope and Definitions – applies to all coursework (e.g., CS 301, MATH 210, HIST 115) and research activities conducted on campus or remotely. The policy clarifies that “plagiarism” includes unattributed use of any copyrighted or non‑copyrighted material, while “cheating” covers the use of unauthorized aids during assessments. Section 2.0 – Prevention Measures – requires faculty to incorporate integrity statements in syllabi, use plagiarism detection software (Turnitin, 2024‑2025 version), and conduct workshops at the start of each semester. Section 3.0 – Reporting and Investigation – establishes the Academic Integrity Committee (AIC), chaired by Dr. Elaine McCarthy (Dean of Academic Affairs), with representation from the Faculty Senate, Student Council, and the Office of Student Services. The AIC meets quarterly (April, July, October, December) and is empowered to review case files, conduct hearings, and recommend sanctions ranging from warning letters to dismissal, depending on the severity and recurrence of violations.

Section 4.0 – Appeals Process – allows students to appeal decisions within 14 days of the AIC’s written determination. Appeals are heard by the Academic Appeals Board, composed of the Provost, the Dean of Students, and an external academic integrity expert. The policy also specifies that all findings and disciplinary actions are recorded in the University’s Academic Integrity Database (ID 2024‑AID‑00123) and are subject to audit by the Office of Institutional Research. The University reaffirms its commitment to fostering a culture of honesty, transparency, and accountability, and invites all members of the campus community to engage with this policy through the scheduled orientation sessions and the online Learning Management System.

title: Library Usage Guidelines
content:
The University of Crestwood Library has updated its usage guidelines effective 1 January 2024, in accordance with the Library Services Committee’s 2023‑24 Review (Committee Minutes #LC‑2023‑15). The policy applies to all students, faculty, staff, and community patrons accessing the campus library facilities, digital resources, and study spaces. Section 3.2 of the Library Policies Manual (Revised 2024) specifies that all visitors must register with the Visitor Management System and comply with the “Quiet Study” and “Digital Resource Use” requirements. Any breach of these terms may result in suspension of library privileges, as documented in Case #2024‑LIB‑001, which involved unauthorized audio recording equipment in a designated study room.

For course-based research, faculty may authorize students to use the special collections in the Rare Materials Wing, provided that the request is submitted through the Course Code Request Form (CCRF‑2024) and approved by the Rare Materials Committee (RMC). The RMC meets bi‑monthly; its last meeting (RMC‑2024‑03) approved the new policy on digital scanning limits, capping at 50 pages per session for copyrighted materials. Students must adhere to the “Digital Copying Limits” subsection (Section 4.1) and obtain a waiver if exceeding the limit. The waiver process is governed by the Library Access and Waiver Form (LAW‑2024) and must be completed no later than the end of the semester in which the request is made.

The Library also enforces the “Late Return and Fine” policy (Section 5.3) to maintain resource availability. Items returned after the due date accrue fines of $0.25 per day, up to a maximum of $5.00 per item. Fines are automatically applied to the borrower’s university account and may affect the borrower’s eligibility to renew or borrow additional materials. The University’s Finance Office will review any fine disputes submitted through the Fine Dispute Form (FDF‑2024) within 30 days of receipt. All policies are posted on the library website (https://library.crestwood.edu/policies) and are available in print at the main desk and the circulation desk on the first floor of the Library Building (B‑101).

title: Academic Calendar 2025-26
content:
The Academic Calendar for the 2025‑26 academic year has been finalized by the Academic Affairs Committee (AAC) following the review of the 2024‑25 schedule and the recent changes to the faculty workload policy. The new calendar reflects a 15‑week fall semester (August 18 – December 12, 2025) and a 12‑week spring semester (January 7 – April 29, 2026), with the Spring Break falling on February 19‑25, 2026. The Fall and Spring Commencement ceremonies will be held on December 16, 2025, and May 5, 2026, respectively, in the University Memorial Auditorium.

Key policy updates include the adoption of the revised Course Code Allocation System (CCAS), effective July 1, 2025. Under CCAS, all new courses must be assigned a unique code beginning with the department abbreviation followed by a four‑digit number (e.g., BIO‑2301 for “Advanced Molecular Biology”). The Office of the Registrar will issue a weekly schedule of available codes in the “Course Code Bulletin” posted on the university intranet. Additionally, the Faculty Workload Committee (FWC) has approved a new “Hybrid Teaching Ratio” of 60 % online, 40 % in‑person for all courses above level 300, to be implemented beginning Fall 2025. Faculty must submit a teaching load report by the 15th of each month for the preceding semester, and any deviations must be justified in writing to the FWC Chair, Dr. L. Nguyen, and recorded in the Faculty Workload Log (Case #FW-2025-07).

Academic calendar updates are communicated through the University Learning Management System (LMS) and the official university email distribution list. The Calendar is available for download in PDF and Microsoft Office formats on the Academic Affairs web portal under “Documents → Academic Calendar 2025‑26.” All students, faculty, and staff are encouraged to review the document and note the important dates for registration, add/drop periods, and exam schedules. The Academic Calendar is a living document; any amendments will be posted within 48 hours of approval by the AAC and communicated via the university’s official channels.

title: Hostel Accommodation Rules
content:
The University of Midvale’s Residential Life Office has adopted the following Hostel Accommodation Rules for the 2024‑2025 academic year. These rules apply to all students residing in the campus‑owned hostels (H1, H2, H3) and are effective from September 1, 2024. The policy is overseen by the Housing and Facilities Committee (HFC), meeting monthly on the first Wednesday of each month at 10:00 AM in Room 204 of the Student Services Building. All changes to these rules must receive HFC approval and be published on the university’s internal portal within 48 hours.

Section 1 – Eligibility and Application: Students must be enrolled in at least 12 credit hours and have completed a successful orientation session by August 15, 2024. Applications for hostel accommodation are submitted electronically through the Housing Portal and are reviewed by the Accommodation Sub‑Committee (ASC). The ASC will assign rooms based on roommate compatibility, academic schedule, and any documented medical or accessibility needs. The committee will issue a formal accommodation letter (Case #2024‑HLC‑001) within 10 business days of receipt of the application.

Section 2 – Conduct and Use of Facilities: All residents are expected to maintain a quiet study environment, respecting the “Quiet Hours” policy (10:00 PM – 7:00 AM) and the “No Smoking” policy in all common areas. Violations of these conduct rules may result in a written warning, followed by a possible suspension of hostel privileges after three infractions within a 12‑month period. The ASC will convene an “Incident Review” meeting within 5 business days of any reported violation, and the outcome will be documented in the Incident Log (e.g., Log Entry #2024‑HLC‑045).

Section 3 – Maintenance and Reporting: Residents must report any maintenance issues via the Housing Portal within 24 hours of discovery. The Facilities Maintenance Team will respond within 48 hours and provide a ticket number (e.g., Ticket #FM‑2024‑HLC‑003). All maintenance requests will be tracked in the university’s Maintenance Management System (MMMS) and resolved in accordance with the “Maintenance Response Time” guidelines (Tier 1: 24 hrs, Tier 2: 72 hrs). Students are encouraged to participate in the annual “Resident Feedback Survey” (Survey #2024‑HF‑FS) to improve hostel services.

These rules are designed to ensure a safe, respectful, and academically conducive living environment for all students. Any questions or clarifications can be directed to the Residential Life Office at reslife@midvale.edu or by calling Extension +1‑555‑123‑4567.

title: Examination Rules and Regulations
content:
All students enrolled in the 2024‑2025 academic year must adhere to the Examination Rules and Regulations as outlined below. The Academic Examinations Committee (AEC), chaired by Dr. Miriam Patel (Chair, AEC), convened on 12 March 2024 to finalize the policy. The committee’s mandate, as per the University Governance Act §3.5, is to ensure fairness, academic integrity, and compliance with national accreditation standards. The policy applies to all courses listed in the 2024‑2025 Undergraduate Catalog (e.g., CS101, HIST210, BIO305, and PHYS402), as well as graduate-level courses (e.g., MBA401, LAW501). 

Students may request a review of examination content or grading under Section 4.2, provided the request is submitted to the AEC within ten (10) days of the published grade. The review process will be handled by a subcommittee consisting of two faculty members and one student representative, with the final decision recorded in the AEC Minutes (Case No. 2024‑AEC‑015). Any appeal must be accompanied by a signed statement of the alleged irregularity, a copy of the relevant exam question(s), and evidence supporting the claim. The AEC will convene a hearing no later than 15 days after receipt of the appeal and issue a written decision within 30 days of the hearing.  

Examination schedules are released on the university’s internal portal by 5 April 2024 for the Fall semester and by 3 October 2024 for the Spring semester. All examinations must be conducted in designated rooms (e.g., Room B‑103 for CS101, Room C‑210 for HIST210) with the prescribed seating chart approved by the AEC. Electronic devices, including smartphones and smartwatches, are prohibited in exam halls unless specifically authorized by the AEC for a particular course (e.g., CALC301, which allows a calculator with a pre‑approved model list). The policy also requires that all proctors receive training on the updated academic integrity procedures, with completion certificates filed in the Student Affairs Office by 31 May 2024.  

The University shall enforce these rules with the assistance of the Office of the Registrar and the Academic Integrity Office. Violations, such as cheating or plagiarism, will be addressed under the Student Disciplinary Code §5.1, with sanctions ranging from a formal warning to suspension, depending on the severity and any prior infractions. All students are encouraged to familiarize themselves with this document and to seek clarification from their instructors or the AEC if any aspect of the rules is unclear.

title: Sports Week Announcement
content:
The University of Westbrook Athletics Department invites all students, faculty, and staff to participate in the annual Sports Week, scheduled for Monday, April 22 through Sunday, April 28, 2024. This week-long event will feature a range of activities, including intramural tournaments, fitness workshops, and a keynote address by Dr. Maria Lopez, Director of the College of Physical Education. The event is open to the entire campus community and will be held across multiple venues: the Main Stadium, the Wellness Center, and the Outdoor Recreation Complex. All participants are encouraged to register through the Athletics Portal by March 31; late registrations will be accepted on a first-come, first-served basis until April 15.

The Sports Week program aligns with the University's 2024 Wellness Initiative, specifically Policy Section 4.2.3, which mandates that at least 15% of the campus population engage in organized physical activity each academic year. In keeping with this policy, the Athletics Department has partnered with the Student Health Services Committee (SHSC) to provide free on-site health screenings and hydration stations. Additionally, the Student Fitness Council (SFC), chaired by Professor James Nguyen (Course Code: PE 101), will conduct a series of skill‑building workshops, including “Advanced Basketball Dribbling” (Course Code: PE 202) and “Yoga for Athletes” (Course Code: PE 303). All workshops are free of charge and will be held in the Wellness Center’s Level 3 Gym from 10:00 AM to 12:00 PM.

Participants are reminded to adhere to the University’s COVID-19 Safety Protocol (Policy Section 7.1.5) during all events. Masks are required in indoor spaces, and proof of vaccination or a negative test result must be presented at the entrance to the Main Stadium. For those who wish to compete, the intramural registration form will include a waiver signed in accordance with Case Number 2024-07, which outlines liability and injury release provisions. Should any conflicts arise, the Athletics Department will coordinate with the Student Legal Services Office (Case Number 2024-12) to ensure compliance with all applicable regulations. We look forward to a week of healthy competition, community building, and celebration of athletic excellence across the University of Westbrook campus.

title: Fee Payment Deadlines and Late Fees Policy
content:
The University of Central Plains’ Finance and Administration Office has adopted the Fee Payment Deadlines and Late Fees Policy (Policy #FAP-2024-07) effective July 1, 2024, to standardize tuition, housing, and activity fee collections across all academic units. Under Section 2.1, the Academic Calendar Committee (ACC) has set the final tuition deadline for the Fall 2024 semester as August 15, 2024. Late payments made between August 16 and September 4 incur a $35 flat late fee, while payments after September 5 incur a 5 % per‑month interest charge on the outstanding balance. The ACC has approved a waiver protocol (Section 3.3) for students with documented financial hardship; requests must be submitted to the Student Financial Services Office (SFSO) by September 1 and will be reviewed by the Student Aid Committee (SAC) within five business days.

Housing fees are governed by Section 4.2 of the Policy, with the Residential Life Committee (RLC) setting the deadline at July 31, 2024 for the 2024–2025 academic year. Late housing payments are subject to a $50 flat penalty, and the RLC has introduced an automated reminder system that will trigger an email on August 5 and a final notice on August 12. The policy references Case #HL-2024-02, wherein a student’s late housing payment resulted in a $120 penalty that was later reduced by 25 % after the student demonstrated a temporary loss of income. This precedent underscores the RLC’s commitment to equitable enforcement.

The University Appeals Board (UAB) will adjudicate any disputes arising from the application of this policy. Appeals must be filed in writing by October 15, 2024, and will be considered under Section 5.1, which mandates a review within 30 calendar days of receipt. The Finance and Administration Office will maintain an electronic log of all fee payments and late fee assessments, accessible to the ACC, SAC, and UAB for audit purposes. This policy ensures transparency, consistency, and fairness in fee collection while providing clear avenues for remediation and appeal.

content:

title: Anti-Ragging Policy
content:
The University of Central Valley has adopted the Anti‑Ragging Policy for the academic year 2024‑2025 to ensure the safety and dignity of all students. Effective from 1 September 2024, the policy applies to all registered students, faculty, staff, and visitors on campus. The Student Welfare Committee (SWC), chaired by Dr. A. N. Patel, Chair of the Department of Psychology, is responsible for monitoring compliance, investigating complaints, and recommending sanctions. All incidents must be reported to the SWC via the online portal (https://uvcv.edu/anti-ragging) or by calling 555‑123‑4567 within 48 hours of the event.

The policy defines ragging as any act or threat of intimidation, harassment, or physical assault that causes emotional or psychological distress. Specific prohibited activities include forced consumption of alcohol, forced participation in humiliating challenges, and any form of physical assault. Case numbers (e.g., AR‑2024‑001, AR‑2024‑023) will be assigned by the SWC for every report. The SWC will conduct a preliminary assessment within 72 hours, and if the evidence warrants, a full investigation will be conducted by the Office of the Registrar in conjunction with the campus police. Sanctions range from formal warnings (for first‑time offenses) to suspension or expulsion for repeat offenders, as stipulated in Section 4.3 of the policy. Affected students may file an appeal within 14 days of the decision, which will be reviewed by the Academic Integrity Board.

The policy also outlines preventive measures: mandatory orientation on 15 August 2024 for all first‑year students, including a 90‑minute workshop titled “Respect & Safety on Campus” led by the Student Affairs Office; mandatory training for faculty and staff on 1 October 2024; and quarterly seminars on campus safety. All course codes (e.g., CS101, BIO202, PHIL303) will be required to display a visible “No Ragging” banner in classrooms and labs. The university encourages a culture of respect and promptly addresses any violations to maintain a safe learning environment for all.

title: Student Grievance Redressal Procedure
content:
The Student Grievance Redressal Procedure (SGRP) outlined below applies to all students of Greenfield University (GUF) for the academic year 2024‑2025. The policy is governed by Section 3.2 of the University Student Handbook and is effective from 1 January 2024. All grievances must be submitted in writing via the online portal (sgp.guf.ac.uk) or by certified mail to the Office of Student Affairs, P.O. Box 1234, Greenfield, GA 90210. The deadline for filing a grievance is 60 days from the date of the incident or decision that is the subject of the complaint.

A student may file a grievance under one of the following categories: (a) Academic Assessment (course codes: BCS 101, BCS 102, BCS 202, BCS 305, BCS 410); (b) Disciplinary Action (e.g., code of conduct violations); (c) Housing or Accommodation; or (d) General Administrative Matters. The student must provide the case number (if already assigned), a clear statement of the issue, supporting documentation (e.g., exam scripts, email correspondence, housing lease, etc.), and any witnesses. The initial review will be conducted by the Student Grievance Officer (SGO), who will issue a written acknowledgement within 5 business days, indicating whether the grievance will be referred to the Student Grievance Committee (SGC) or resolved at the SGO level.

The SGC, chaired by the Dean of Student Affairs, convenes bi‑weekly (Mondays at 2:00 pm) in Room 402, Administration Building. The committee consists of the SGO, a faculty representative from the relevant department, a member of the Student Representative Council, and a legal counsel from the university’s Office of Legal Services. The SGC will hold a hearing no later than 30 days after the SGO’s referral. The hearing will be conducted in a confidential manner, with the student, any witnesses, and relevant staff present. After deliberation, the SGC will issue a decision in writing within 14 days of the hearing, which will be communicated to all parties involved. The decision will reference the applicable policy sections (e.g., § 5.1 for grading disputes, § 6.3 for disciplinary matters) and will provide a clear rationale for the outcome, including any remedial actions or appeals. All decisions are final unless an appeal is filed with the Office of the Provost within 10 business days of receipt of the SGC decision.

title: IT Lab Usage Policy
content:
The University of Midvale’s Information Technology Services (ITS) has adopted this IT Lab Usage Policy to govern all use of campus computer labs during the 2024‑2025 academic year. The policy is effective July 1, 2024 and applies to all students, faculty, staff, and contractors who access the lab facilities located in Building 3 (Laboratory 301, 302, and 303). The policy is reviewed annually by the ITS Governance Committee, chaired by Dr. Elena Martinez, and any amendments are documented in the ITS Policy Register (reference ITS‑POL‑2024‑01). The policy is publicly available on the university’s intranet under the “Information Technology Services” section and is also archived in the university’s public policy repository (https://midvale.edu/policies/itlab).

Section 1 – Access and Identification. Only individuals with a valid university identification card and an active IT Services account may enter the labs. Guests must be escorted by a registered user and may only remain for a maximum of two hours per session. Each user must log in to the lab’s Wi‑Fi network using their university credentials and must accept the ITS Acceptable Use Agreement before using any lab equipment. Violations of this requirement are reported to the ITS Security Team and may result in temporary or permanent revocation of lab access, as documented in case number ITS‑SEC‑2024‑045.

Section 2 – Equipment and Resource Management. Lab computers are designated for academic work only. The use of external storage devices is prohibited unless approved by the ITS Lab Manager, Ms. Aaron Lee. Software installation is strictly prohibited; all software must be pre‑approved and installed by the ITS Help Desk. Users are required to log off all applications and power down their workstation before leaving the lab. Any damage or malfunction must be reported immediately to the lab assistant on duty, whose contact information is posted on the wall near the exit.

Section 3 – Conduct and Security. Users must maintain a professional environment, keeping noise levels below 50 dB and refraining from disruptive behavior. The labs are monitored by a network of CCTV cameras, and recordings are retained for 90 days in compliance with the University Privacy Policy. Any suspicious activity or security breach must be reported to the ITS Incident Response Team (contact: it‑ir@midvale.edu). Repeated violations may result in disciplinary action under the University Code of Conduct (see section 4.2 of the Code) and may be escalated to the Office of Student Affairs.

title: Scholarship Eligibility Criteria
content:
The University of Midvale Scholarship Office has finalized the 2024‑2025 Scholarship Eligibility Criteria, effective from the beginning of the Fall 2024 semester. The criteria were reviewed by the Academic Affairs Committee on 12 March 2024 and approved by the University Senate on 28 April 2024. All applicants must be enrolled in at least 12 credit hours and maintain a cumulative GPA of 3.25 or higher. Applicants whose GPA falls below the threshold may be considered for a conditional scholarship if they demonstrate a minimum of 3.00 GPA in the current semester and have completed at least one of the following remedial courses: BIO101 (Introductory Biology), MATH220 (College Algebra), or ENG201 (Academic Writing). 

Eligibility also requires proof of financial need, verified by the Office of Student Financial Aid through a completed FAFSA or CSS Profile no later than 15 May 2024. Students with a family income below the 30th percentile for the Midvale region, as determined by the Department of Economic Studies, are automatically eligible for the Full‑Need Scholarship. For students with incomes between the 30th and 50th percentiles, the Partial‑Need Scholarship is available, subject to a review by the Financial Aid Committee (FAC) under policy section 4.3.2. The SAC (Scholarship Award Committee) will convene monthly to review applications; the next meeting is scheduled for 2 June 2024.

Case numbers are assigned sequentially by the Scholarship Office. For instance, the most recent applicant, case #2024-0456, was reviewed on 9 May 2024 and received a partial award of $1,200. All decisions are recorded in the University Scholarship Database (USDB) and are available for audit by the Office of Institutional Research. Any appeals must be submitted in writing to the Appeals Board by 30 June 2024, citing the relevant policy section and providing supporting documentation. The University remains committed to transparent, equitable scholarship distribution in accordance with the University’s Diversity and Inclusion Charter.

title: National Holiday Revised Schedule
content:
The University of Midvale hereby announces the revised National Holiday schedule for the 2024‑2025 academic year. In accordance with the University Calendar Committee’s 2024‑2025 Calendar Revision Report (URC‑2024‑05) and in compliance with the State Education Act § 12.3(b)(i), the following adjustments apply to all academic units, including graduate research programs and continuing education courses.

title: Dress Code and Campus Conduct Policy
content:
The University of Westbridge has adopted the Dress Code and Campus Conduct Policy effective July 1, 2024. The policy applies to all students, faculty, staff, and contractors on the Main, East, and West campuses. Section A.1 clarifies that attire must be “appropriate for a professional academic environment.” This includes prohibitions on clothing with offensive slogans, revealing garments (e.g., crop tops, shorts below the knee for students, sleeveless tops for faculty), and clothing that could be considered a distraction during instructional activities. The policy cites the 2023 “Campus Safety Review” report (Report No. CS‑23‑07) and aligns with the Ohio State Higher Education Act § 5.6, ensuring consistency with state regulations.

Section B.2 addresses specific course codes: for all courses listed in the Academic Calendar (e.g., BIO 101, PSY 210, ART 301), instructors must enforce the dress code during labs, recitations, and in‑class activities. The Student Conduct Committee (SCC), chaired by Dr. Maria Gonzalez, has reviewed 12 cases (Case Nos. SCC‑2024‑03, SCC‑2024‑11, SCC‑2024‑27) where students were cited for non‑compliance. Each case resulted in a formal warning and a required participation in the “Campus Culture Workshop” scheduled for September 15, 2024. Faculty members are instructed to document violations in the Campus Conduct Log (CL‑2024‑05) and to notify the Dean of Student Affairs within 48 hours.

Section C.3 establishes an enforcement procedure. A first offense incurs a verbal warning and a written notice. A second offense results in a mandatory meeting with the SCC and possible suspension of campus privileges for up to one week. Repeat violations may lead to a formal hearing before the University Disciplinary Board, with the possibility of dismissal of enrollment. The policy is reviewed annually by the University Policies and Governance Committee (PPGC), which met on March 28, 2025 to approve the 2025‑2026 revision. All stakeholders are encouraged to familiarize themselves with the full policy text, available on the University’s internal portal under “Student Affairs > Policies.”

title: Medical Facilities on Campus
content:
The University Health Services (UHS) has reviewed and approved the updated “Medical Facilities on Campus” policy effective 1 October 2024. This policy consolidates the campus-wide guidelines for the use, maintenance, and safety of all medical facilities, including the Student Health Center (SHC), the Athletic Training Facility (ATF), and the Emergency Response Stations (ERS) located at the North, South, and East Halls. The policy supersedes the 2019 version and incorporates the findings of the Health & Safety Committee (HSC) review conducted on 15 March 2024, with the final amendment signed by the Vice President for Student Affairs on 27 September 2024.

Section 3.1 outlines the required licensing and inspection schedule: all medical facilities must undergo an annual inspection by the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) under case number DHHS‑24‑0042, and the results must be submitted to the UHS Compliance Office within 30 days of the inspection. The policy also specifies that each facility must maintain a minimum of 12 hours of on‑site medical coverage per week, with a documented shift rotation plan approved by the UHS Medical Advisory Board (MAB) no later than 15 January 2025. For the SHC, the new course code MED‑HSS‑102 (Campus Health Management) will provide training to student volunteers on proper triage procedures, and all volunteers must complete this course before their first shift.

Section 4.2 addresses emergency protocols, detailing the response times for ERS activation. The policy requires that all ERS stations be equipped with a fully functional Automated External Defibrillator (AED) and that a bi‑annual simulation drill be conducted in collaboration with the campus fire department. The University’s Incident Response Team (IRT) will log each drill under incident number IRT‑25‑001 and review outcomes in the quarterly IRT meeting held on the first Friday of each month. The policy also mandates that any medical incident involving a student or staff member be reported to the Office of Student Conduct within 24 hours, and the incident will be assigned a unique case number for tracking and audit purposes.

title: Parking and Transportation Policy
content:
Effective July 1, 2024, the University of Midvale’s Transportation and Parking Committee (TPC) adopts the following Parking and Transportation Policy to streamline campus mobility, reduce congestion, and support sustainable commuting options. Section 1.1 outlines the campus parking zones: Zone A (North Campus, 200 spaces), Zone B (South Campus, 150 spaces), and Zone C (Administrative Complex, 100 spaces). All vehicles must display a valid “Midvale Parking Permit” (MP-2024-XX) issued by the Student Services Office (SSO) and are subject to a $50 monthly fee. Violations—including unauthorized parking in restricted areas—will trigger a $100 fine (Case MP-2024-001) and, for repeat offenders, a 30‑day revocation of parking privileges.

Section 2.2 establishes the “Transit Pass” program for faculty, staff, and graduate students, providing a free monthly pass for local bus routes 12, 15, and 18. Passes are distributed through the Faculty and Staff Office (FSO) and expire on September 30, 2024, with renewal available through the same office. In addition, the TPC encourages carpooling by offering a discounted “Carpool Permit” (CP-2024-XX) for vehicles carrying three or more occupants. This permit is issued by the Transportation Services Department (TSD) and is valid until December 31, 2024. All permits must be renewed annually; failure to renew results in a $25 penalty (Case CP-2024-003).

Section 3.3 addresses bike and pedestrian safety. The university has installed 30 new bike racks across campus, with 10 additional racks added on August 15, 2024, in response to the “Bike Safety Initiative” (BSI‑2024-04) submitted by the Student Union Bike Committee. Pedestrian pathways will be resurfaced by May 31, 2025, as part of the “Safe Walkways Project” (SWP‑2024-07). The policy also requires all new construction projects to include a minimum of two bicycle parking spaces per 500 square feet of office space, as mandated by the Office of Sustainability (OOS) under Resolution 2024‑05.

The TPC will review this policy annually, with the next review scheduled for June 30, 2025. All updates will be posted on the university’s official website (www.midvale.edu/parking) and communicated through campus email alerts. This policy supersedes all prior parking regulations issued before July 1, 2024.

title: Disciplinary Hearing Minutes – Plagiarism Case A
content:
On 14 March 2025, the Academic Integrity Committee of the School of Computer Science convened at 10:30 AM in Room B‑204 to conduct a disciplinary hearing under Case No. A‑2025‑PLAG‑01. The committee, chaired by Dr. Kavita Deshmukh, Associate Dean for Student Affairs, was joined by committee members Prof. S. R. Patel, Chair of the Computer Science Department, and Dr. Arun Mehta, Director of the Academic Integrity Office. The hearing was attended by the student accused of plagiarism, Ananya Verma (Roll No. RK3P25KZB01, email: ananya.rk3p25kzb01@university.edu), her assigned mentor Dr. Nikhil Rao, and a student representative, Priya Nair (Roll No. RK3P25KZB42, email: priya.rk3p25kzb42@university.edu). The allegation concerns the submission of the term project for Course CS‑305 (Advanced Algorithms) submitted on 2 February 2025. The proposal is based on the findings of the 2024 salary survey conducted by the HR Analytics Team, which revealed that the current base salaries for faculty in the College of Engineering and the College of Humanities are below the 25th percentile of comparable institutions in the region. Accordingly, the CBC recommends a 12.5 % increase for all full‑time tenure‑track faculty effective 1 July 2025, with a phased implementation for adjunct and part‑time staff to be reviewed in the 2026 academic year.

Key details of the proposal include:

- **Eligibility and Scope** – The increase applies to all tenure‑track professors, associate professors, and assistant professors across the College of Engineering (codes EE‑101 to EE‑105) and the College of Humanities (codes HUM‑201 to HUM‑205). Adjuncts (codes ADJ‑301 to ADJ‑305) will receive a 7 % adjustment, subject to budgetary constraints.
- **Budget Impact** – The total projected cost for the 2025 academic year is ₹1.2 Cr, which is within the allocated Faculty Compensation Reserve of ₹1.5 Cr. A detailed cost breakdown is attached as Annex A.
- **Implementation Timeline** – Effective dates, payroll adjustments, and notification procedures are outlined in Annex B. All faculty will receive a formal letter by 15 June 2025.
- **Compliance and Reporting** – The proposal aligns with the University’s Equal Pay Policy (Section 4.3, 2023) and the National Institute for Teacher Salary Standards (NITSS) guidelines. Annual reporting to the Ministry of Education will be updated accordingly.

The CBC has consulted with the Faculty Union (FU‑2024), who have provided feedback on the proposed increase. The union’s representative, Ms. Priya Nair (Roll No.: RK3P25KZB08, Email: priya.rk3p25kzb08@university.edu), has endorsed the proposal contingent upon the inclusion of a cost‑of‑living adjustment clause. The final draft is ready for executive review on 30 June 2025.

title: External Audit Findings – Finance Department
content:
The Finance Department audit for the 2024‑25 academic year has been completed by the Internal Audit Committee on 15 March 2025. The audit, conducted under the guidelines of the University Financial Management Policy (UFMP) Section 3.4 and the Internal Controls Manual (ICM) Chapter 7, identified a total of 12 discrepancies in the disbursement of grant funds for the School of Social Sciences. Case numbers are listed in Appendix A and are referenced herein for further action.

Key findings include the following: (1) An unauthorized transfer of ₹2,50,000 from the Student Development Fund to the research grant account for project CS2024‑05 was recorded on 02 February 2025. The transfer was signed by Finance Officer Rohan Sharma (roll RK3P25KZB12) but was not approved by the Finance Committee Chair, Ms. Priya Nair (roll RK3P25KZB07). (2) The allocation of ₹1,80,000 to the “Student Research Grants” (course code SSG‑2025) was approved by the Grants Committee but the supporting documentation was missing for the student Ananya Verma (roll RK3P25KZB01) and her project “Digital Literacy in Rural Schools.” (3) The audit found that the monthly reconciliation of the University Treasury account was delayed by an average of 18 days over the fiscal year, contravening the Treasury Management Policy (Section 5.2). (4) A discrepancy of ₹75,000 was noted in the disbursement ledger for the “International Exchange Program” (course code IEP‑2024), where the recipient’s email address (ananya.rk3p25kzb01@university.edu) was recorded incorrectly as anapya.rk3p25kzb01@university.edu, leading to a delayed payment to the partner institution in Spain.

Recommendations: The Finance Department must implement a two‑signature requirement for all transfers exceeding ₹1,00,000, as per UFMP Section 3.7. All grant applications must be accompanied by complete documentation before approval. The Treasury reconciliation process should be automated through the Finance Information System (FIS) to ensure weekly reporting. The audit committee will review the implementation of these recommendations in the next quarterly meeting on 20 April 2025.
